title: The longest chains: A needs B, B needs C
question: How many permits and approvals can the published sentences stack one behind another?
finding: The longest string of stated "before" requirements runs 4 steps: Fire alarm permit  needs  Electrical permit  needs  Building permit  needs  Project Application filed with Planning  needs  Pre-application meeting with neighbors. Its links apply only to: solar systems; projects needing intake review, neighbor notice or an entitlement; certain kinds of project. 5 chains reach that length, and 96 start-to-end chains run two steps or more.
how: Each "before" pair is a link. Links are joined wherever the thing one permit needs is itself a permit with its own stated prerequisite. The longest chain is kept for each starting permit and end point.
limits: Every link carries its own condition, so a chain shows the longest path the published sentences could make, not a typical job: a chain through the solar electrical permit applies only to solar work on a project that also needs Planning review. Links stated only in the codes or in PDF forms are missing, which would make real chains longer.
